data.name: Wizard King
data.detailed_description:
Hello Wizard! Are you ready to go on an expedition?
Travelers who have traveled around Nordia have been told that there are various creatures that threaten travelers in Nordia.
But do not worry too much. The more you do magic battles with them, you will be able to create your own powerful deck, collecting magic spells to fight with you, and spells that can be activated when needed.
Good luck with your challenge to be a Wizard King.


Game Play:
Wizard King is a strategy collectible card game. (CCG / TCG)
However, instead of playing cards, you will play the game with real summon creature and magic.
Therefore, you can enjoy more easy and active games than ordinary card games.


Features:
- Over 220 collectible cards

- 160 battle stages vs various opponents

- 40 interesting expedition stages

reviews.review:
[i]Wizard King[/i] is a strategy game that mixes trading card game elements with role playing game elements but sadly falls short on all fronts. There is no story whatsoever here, all you do is play at your leisure to collect new cards and progress in levels. While a game certainly does not need a story to be good, the absence of one took away any sense of urgency to complete the game. The title is single player so all you can do is fight against the AI.  The lack of multiplayer compounded by lack of story left me with little incentive to improve my deck. It helps progress in the game but there is no reward for doing so; not even Steam achievements.

Despite this, the game isn’t horrible to play. There is a tutorial that teaches you most of the basics. Then you can partake in battles to gain new cards to help your deck. There is also an expedition mode but the game warns players to first complete all of the battles before trying it. Gameplay is a bit slow and clunky. You have your main character who must be protected, if he dies then it’s game over, however, the opposition follows the same rules. Using your deck you summon warriors to do battle for you and also cast spells to support your team or attack the enemy. You start off with a very basic, but useful, deck that can probably get you far with very little tweaking. Despite this being a strategy game there isn’t much to be seen, as long as you have enough summon characters to attack you’ll be fine, boosts help as well. Certain enemies require a little bit of a different approach but for the most part it’s all the same.

My biggest issue with the game, that I also feel relates to how slow gameplay can be, is that you can only have five characters on the field at a time. This isn’t a big issue but all the characters stand behind each other in a line. Melee fighters must be in front and ranged ones in the second or third spot and then healers or status boosting characters in the back. Much like in real life, what draws from the deck is random so there is strategy in how you place summons but they attack slowly and only being able to use one single melee characters drags things along since ranged ones aren’t as strong. You also can’t have a summon target anyone so you’re forced to beat down whatever character the enemy has in front until they run out and only their main character is left. You can reshuffle your deck if need be but that costs mana. Summoning costs mana, spells cost mana, changing the position of your characters costs mana… all of this makes mana the most important aspect of the game and it generates slowly.

[i]Wizard King[/i] isn’t a bad game, but it’s painfully mediocre. Graphics aren’t pretty, the gameplay could be better and the English translation at certain points is poor and can confuse players. It is fun to play but not for very long, the title shows promise but sadly doesn’t fully deliver and is easily forgettable in a sea of other collectable trading card games.

[b]Pros[/b]
[list]
    [*]Somewhat affordable.
    [*]Simple gameplay to learn, easy to pick up for short bursts of fun.
    [*]It is fun and some levels can be challenging. 
[/list]

[b]Cons[/b]
[list]
    [*]Gets repetitive very easily.
    [*]Graphics aren’t very good looking at all and the user interface is boring.
    [*]The same music plays over and over again.
[*]The English translation is barely passable. 
[*]No Steam achievements or trading cards.
[/list]
